This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of FIR bearing crime No.62/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali District Gwalior against the petitioner for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 of IPC.
2.

As per prosecution case, the complainant/respondent No.2 lodged the impugend FIR stating that the father and uncle of the complainant had purchased 1854 square feet of land situated near Balabai Ki Chhatri, Hanuman Bandh Nala, Nagar Lashkar, Gwalior, from Smt. Suninda Raje Shitole through a registered sale deed dated 01.10.1995.

After purchasing the said property, a written exchange deed between the complainant's father Rajendra Kumar Jain and his uncle Narendra Kumar Jain was executed and registered on 23.03.2009, pursuant to which the entire 1854 square feet of land came into the share of the complainant's father.

Subsequently, in respect of 1070 square feet of the said land, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 2 MCRC-38858-2023 complainant's father executed a general power of attorney (Mukhtyarnama Aam) in favour of Hemant Pal (present petitioner) on 05.08.2010, authorizing him to sell the said portion of land,
which was duly registered in the office of the Sub- Registrar on the same date.
Furthermore, the complainant's father also executed a written agreement before a notary on 17.08.2010 in favour of Hemant Pal concerning the said 1070 square feet of land.

Thereafter, on 14.08.2012, another written Hemant Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22917131/
1 agreement was executed between the complainant's father and Hemant Pal regarding the remaining 784 square feet of land.

sentences.text: However, under the pretext of getting this agreement registered, two days after the execution of the said agreement, i.e., on 16.08.2012, Hemant Pal took the complainant's father to the Registrar's office and, by deceitfully misleading him, fraudulently prepared a forged general power of attorney for 1070 square feet of land instead of 784 square feet, and obtained his signatures on it, despite the fact that only 784 square feet of land remained in the name of the complainant's father at that time.

On the basis of the said forged general power of attorney, Hemant Pal executed a registered sale deed dated 13.08.2013 transferring 860 square feet of land in the name of his maternal uncle Bharat Baghel, son of Badriprasad Baghel, resident of Daulatganj.
The complainant's father Rajendra Kumar Jain passed away on 17.09.2020 due to COVID-19.

After his demise, when the complainant initiated mutation proceedings in the Municipal Corporation in the year 2020, and while the said mutation process was still pending, Geeta, wife of Vidharam Rathore,
began dismantling the structure (Pataur) situated on the said land, whereupon the complainant came to know that Hemant Pal had fraudulently sold the land to Bharat Baghel on the basis of the forged power of attorney dated 13.08.2013, and Bharat Baghel had subsequently sold the same land to Geeta, wife of Vidharam NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 3 MCRC-38858-2023 Rathore.

Thus, by deceitfully obtaining the signatures of the complainant's father on a forged general power of attorney instead of the intended agreement document and subsequently selling the land, Hemant Pal and Bharat Baghel have committed fraud and forgery.
On the basis of the aforesaid allegations, the present FIR has been registered against the present petitioner and the co-accused person.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned FIR has been registered against the petitioner on wholly incorrect and misconceived facts.

It is contended that the petitioner has neither forged nor fabricated any document; nevertheless, the FIR has been lodged at Police Station Kotwali, Lashkar, District Gwalior (M.P.) on false and misleading allegations.
A bare perusal of the FIR would clearly reveal that it does not disclose the commission of any cognizable offence so far as the petitioner is concerned.
4. It is further submitted that the father of the complainant had executed a valid Power of Attorney in favour of the petitioner in respect of land admeasuring 1070 square feet.
Acting under the authority o the said Power of Attorney, the petitioner had sold only 860 square feet of the said land.
Therefore, the allegation that the petitioner has committed any act of forgery, fabrication, or illegality is wholly baseless and contrary to the record.
5. It is further submitted that the petitioner sold the property on the basis of a valid and duly executed power of attorney.
The said power of attorney was executed by Rajendra Kumar Jain on 12.08.2011 and subsequently another power of attorney was executed on 16.08.2012.
On the basis of the said power of attorney dated 16.08.2012, the petitioner executed a registered sale deed on 13.08.2013.
The power of attorney in question was executed by Late Rajendra Kumar Jain, the father of the complainant, and the same was a duly registered document executed before the competent Registrar.

Therefore, the said document cannot be said to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 4 MCRC-38858-2023 forged or fabricated by the petitioner.

It is also pertinent to note that during his lifetime, Rajendra Kumar Jain never raised any objection nor Hemant Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22917131/
2 lodged any complaint against the petitioner in relation to the said power of attorney or the sale transaction.

sentences.text: 6. It is further contended that the complainant, Prashant Jain, has alleged before the police that the power of attorney dated 16.08.2012 is a forged and manipulated document.

However, it is important to note that Rajendra Kumar Jain expired on 17.09.2020 and during his lifetime neither he nor the present complainant ever raised any grievance or made any complaint against the petitioner with regard to the alleged forgery.

After a lapse of more than eight years from the execution of the sale deed, the complainant has lodged the present complaint on incorrect and baseless grounds, which clearly demonstrates that the FIR has been filed as an afterthought.
7. It is also submitted that for the applicability of Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, the essential ingredients of cheating as defined under Section 415 IPC must be satisfied.
There must be a dishonest intention from the very inception and deception resulting in delivery of property.
In the present case, the complaint as well as the FIR does not disclose any such ingredient.
There is nothing in the complaint nor in the documents relied upon by the complainant to indicate that the petitioner had deceived or cheated anyone within the meaning of Section 415 IPC.
Consequently, no prima facie case under Section 420 IPC is made out against the petitioner.

8. It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that a bare perusal of the FIR clearly reveals that the dispute between the parties is essentially of a civil nature, which has deliberately been given the colour of a criminal proceeding.

Even if the allegations made in the complaint are assumed to be true NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 5 MCRC-38858-2023 for the sake of argument, the appropriate remedy available to the complainant is to approach the competent civil court for cancellation of the alleged sale deed or to challenge the validity of the Power of Attorney.

It is pertinent to mention that the complainant himself has already instituted a civil suit bearing No. 390/2022 on 20.04.2022 seeking a declaration that the Power of Attorney dated 16.08.2012, allegedly executed by the petitioner by deceitfully misleading and conspiring against the complainant's father, is null and void.

The complainant has further prayed that the Sale Deed dated 13.08.2013, executed on the basis of the said Power of Attorney, as well as the subsequent Sale Deed dated 11.11.2021 executed by Bharat Baghel in favour of Smt. Geeta Rathore and registered on 12.11.2021, be declared null and void.

However, it is significant to note that despite making allegations of deceit and forgery, no document or material whatsoever indicating any act of forgery has been filed by the complainant along with the said civil suit.
This clearly demonstrates that the allegations raised in the FIR are an attempt to give a criminal colour to a dispute which is otherwise purely civil in nature.

9. It is thus submitted that the present FIR is nothing but an attempt by the complainant to question the validity of a duly registered power of attorney and a registered sale deed after an inordinate delay.

The complainant himself admits that his father had executed a power of attorney in favour of the petitioner in respect of 1070 sq. ft. area and thereafter executed another power of attorney for the remaining 784 sq. ft.
Despite these transactions, Rajendra Kumar Jain continued to live for several years thereafter and never raised any objection.

The long silence on the part of the executant of the power of attorney clearly establishes that the present allegations are false, fabricated and Hemant Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22917131/
3 concocted.

The impugned FIR, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 6 MCRC-38858-2023 therefore, deserves to be quashed as it is nothing but an abuse of the process of law.
10.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the petition and submitted that the impugned FIR clearly discloses the commission of cognizable offences and, therefore, the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. ought not to be invoked at this stage.

It is contended that the allegations made in the complaint, when taken at their face value,
specifically state that the petitioner, by deceitfully misrepresenting the nature of the document,
obtained the signatures of the complainant's father on a General Power of Attorney for 1070 square feet of land instead of 784 square feet and thereafter, on the basis of the said document, executed a registered sale deed in favour of a close relative.
Such allegations prima facie disclose ingredients of offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of IPC.

It is further submitted that whether the power of attorney was obtained by deception, whether the document was forged or manipulated,
and whether the petitioner acted with dishonest intention are all questions of fact which require thorough investigation and cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C. at the threshold.

The State further submits that merely because the complainant has also availed civil remedies or instituted a civil suit does not bar criminal proceedings when the allegations disclose elements of cheating and forgery.
The delay in lodging the complaint and the defence raised by the petitioner are matters of evidence which can be examined during investigation or trial.

Thus, the petition seeking quashment of FIR deserves to be dismissed.
11.

Learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.2 also opposed the petition and submitted that the present petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is wholly misconceived and deserves to be dismissed at the threshold as the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 7 MCRC-38858-2023 impugned FIR clearly discloses the commission of cognizable offences.

It is contended that the allegations made in the complaint specifically state that the petitioner, by deceitfully misrepresenting the nature of the document, obtained the signatures of the complainant's father on a General Power of Attorney for 1070 square feet of land instead of 784 square feet and thereafter,
on the basis of the said forged document, executed a registered Sale Deed dated 13.08.2013 in favour of his close relative, thereby causing wrongful loss to the complainant and his family.
Such allegations, when taken at their face value, clearly satisfy the essential ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is further submitted that the questions as to whether the Power of Attorney was obtained by deception, whether the document was manipulated, and whether the petitioner acted with dishonest and fraudulent intention are disputed questions of fact which require detailed investigation and appreciation of evidence and therefore cannot be adjudicated in the limited jurisdiction exercised by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. at the stage of quashment of FIR.

12. Learned counsel further submits that merely because a civil suit has also been instituted by the complainant seeking declaration and cancellation of the impugned documents does not bar criminal prosecution when the allegations disclose elements of cheating and forgery.
It is well settled that civil and criminal remedies may proceed simultaneously when the allegations constitute a criminal offence.

Accordingly, it is submitted that the present petition is nothing but an attempt by the Hemant Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22917131/
4 petitioner to stifle a legitimate prosecution and to thwart a fair investigation.

Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

14. The gravamen of the allegations contained in the impugned FIR primarily pertains to the execution and validity of a General Power of Attorney and the subsequent sale deed executed on the basis thereof.

The dispute essentially arises from the complainant's allegation that the petitioner, by deceitfully misleading his father, fraudulently prepared a forged General Power of Attorney for land admeasuring 1070 square feet, instead of 784 square feet, and obtained his signatures thereon.
It is further alleged that, on the strength of the said document, the petitioner subsequently executed a registered sale deed in favour of a third party.
15. At this stage it is necessary to examine whether the allegations made in the FIR satisfy the essential ingredients of the offences alleged.
The offence of cheating punishable under Section 420 of IPC is founded upon the definition of "cheating" contained in Section 415 of IPC.

In order to constitute an offence of cheating there must be a dishonest or fraudulent intention on the part of the accused at the very inception of the transaction and such deception must induce the person so deceived to deliver property or to do or omit to do something which he would not have done or omitted if he were not so deceived.
16. In the present case, the allegations contained in the FIR do not disclose that the petitioner had any dishonest intention at the inception of the transaction.
The documents forming the basis of the transaction, namely the Power of Attorney and the subsequent sale deed, are registered documents executed before the competent authority.

The executant of the Power of Attorney, namely Rajendra Kumar Jain, remained alive for several years after the execution of these documents and admittedly did not raise any grievance or initiate any proceedings NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 9 MCRC-38858-2023 alleging fraud or deception during his lifetime.
The absence of any such allegation by the executant himself for a considerable period of time creates a serious doubt regarding the allegation of deception at the inception.
17. Moreover, the dispute raised by the complainant essentially relates to the validity and effect of the Power of Attorney and the consequential sale deed.
Such issues are primarily matters for adjudication by a civil court.
In fact, the complainant himself has already instituted a civil suit seeking declaration that the Power of Attorney dated 16.08.2012 and the sale deeds executed pursuant thereto are null and void.
The existence of such civil proceedings further indicates that the controversy between the parties pertains to the civil rights arising out of property transactions.
18. So far as the offences under Sections 467 and 468 of IPC are concerned, the essential ingredient of these provisions is the making of a false document with intent to cause damage or injury.

The FIR does not disclose any material showing that the petitioner fabricated or forged the document in Hemant Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22917131/
5 question.

sentences.text: The document alleged to be forged is a registered instrument executed before the Sub-Registrar and there is no specific allegation supported by material indicating that the petitioner himself created a false document or impersonated the executant.

A mere allegation that the complainant's father was misled at the time of execution, without any supporting circumstances or material, is not sufficient to attract the offences of forgery as contemplated under Sections 467 and 468 of IPC.
19.

It is well settled that though the power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is to be exercised sparingly,
the Court is empowered to quash criminal proceedings

where the allegations contained in the FIR,
even if taken at their face value, do not constitute the offence alleged and where the continuation of such proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of law.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7940 10 MCRC-38858-2023 20.

In the facts of the present case, this Court is of the considered view that the allegations made in the FIR primarily relate to a dispute regarding the validity of a power of attorney and a sale deed executed on the basis thereof.
The essential ingredients of cheating as defined under Section 415 IPC and punishable under Section 420 IPC are not made out.
Similarly, the material available on record does not prima facie disclose the commission of offences of forgery punishable under Sections 467 and 468 of IPC.
In such circumstances, permitting the criminal proceedings to continue would amount to giving a criminal colour to what is essentially a civil dispute between the parties.
21. Accordingly, this Court finds that the present case is a fit case for exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Consequently, the petition is allowed.

The FIR bearing Crime No. 62/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Gwalior for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of the Indian Penal Code, and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom against the present petitioner, are hereby quashed.
22.
The petition stands disposed of accordingly.
